title: Portable Agent Memory: A Protocol for Cryptographically-Verified Memory Transfer Across Heterogeneous AI Agents
abstract: We present Portable Agent Memory, an open protocol and reference implementation for transferring persistent memory state across heterogeneous AI agents. abstract: Robust optimization (RO) provides a principled framework for decision-making under uncertainty, but its practical use is often limited by the need to manually reformulate uncertain optimization models into tractable deterministic counterparts. abstract: Memory data are ubiquitous in Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents (e.g., OpenClaw and Manus). abstract: Long-form technical report (~36,000 words) developing the axiomatic foundation of agent memory in partial Horn logic. title: Visual Agentic Memory: Enabling Online Long Video Understanding via Online Indexing, Hierarchical Memory, and Agentic Retrieval
abstract: Long video understanding requires more than large context windows. It also needs a memory mechanism that decides what visual evidence to retain, keeps it searchable over long horizons, and grounds later reasoning in recoverable observations rather than compressed latent state alone. title: ParaCell: Paravirtualized Secure Containers with Lightweight Intra-Container Isolation and Intent-Driven Memory Management
abstract: Secure containers isolate each container with its own kernel, mitigating shared-kernel attacks prevalent in traditional container systems. However, existing designs still face a fundamental isolation--performance trade-off. title: Collaborative LLM Agents for End-to-End Software Development
abstract: This tutorial explores the next generation of AI-powered software development, where large language models (LLMs) function as collaborative agents that plan, code, test, and review alongside human developers. title: ExpGraph: Model-Agnostic Experience Learning with Graph-Structured Memory for LLM Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown strong capabilities in reasoning, tool use, and multi-step interaction, but they often solve tasks from scratch and fail to reuse successful strategies or failure lessons from prior experience. abstract: Matrix Context: Mixture-of-Contexts RAG for Robust and Inspectable Agent Memory We introduce Mixture-of-Contexts RAG (MoC-RAG), a routed retrieval architecture for agent memory that selects a small set of typed context experts before retrieving, then assembles a token-budgeted, inspectable context pack. title: The Governance Gap in Agentic Memory
abstract: The Governance Gap in Agentic Memory - a position paper proposing Substrate-Lens-Frame (SLF), a sovereign, auditable memory protocol for AI agents. AI agents now run on persistent memory, and that memory has become its own layer in the stack. title: Agent Memory: Characterization and System Implications of Stateful Long-Horizon Workloads
abstract: LLM agents are increasingly deployed on long-horizon tasks requiring sustained reasoning over extended interaction histories. Realizing this at scale requires agents to persistently store, retrieve, and update their own memory across sessions. A rich ecosystem of agent memory systems has emerged spanning flat retrieval, LLM-mediated extraction, consolidating fact stores, and agentic control flows.

title: Continual Learning Bench: Evaluating Frontier AI Systems in Real-World Stateful Environments
abstract: Continual learning, the ability of AI systems to improve through sequential experience, has attracted substantial interest, but no high-quality benchmark exists to evaluate it. We introduce Continual Learning Bench (CL-Bench), the first difficult, expert-validated benchmark designed to measure whether LLM-based systems genuinely improve with experience. title: Evaluation of long-term memory methods for large language models as conversational agents
abstract: The ability of Large Language Models to perform as autonomous conversational agents is fundamentally constrained by the fixed context window of the transformer architecture. title: One of Us or One of Them? The Effect of Social Categorization on Agent Memory
abstract: This research investigates the bidirectional relationship between linguistic framing and social categorization in the context of eyewitness memory. Building on Fausey and Boroditsky (2010), who demonstrated cross-linguistic differences in agent memory for accidental events between English and Spanish speakers, this two-study proposal extends their findings in two directions. abstract: Key-Value (KV) cache memory management has become a central engineering challenge in long-context large language model (LLM) inference, with cache consumption growing linearly with sequence length and, in documented cases, coming to dominate GPU memory over static model parameters. title: UserCentrix: An Agentic Memory-augmented AI Framework for Smart Spaces
abstract: Agentic AI, with its autonomous and proactive decision-making, has transformed smart environments.
